title: A Preregistered Audit of Dataset Contamination Controls in LLM-for-NetOps Benchmarks
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired, confirmatory audit that applied conservative deterministic contamination detectors (exact normalized-token equality; fuzzy 5‑gram overlap; provenance heuristics) and a guarded exclusion policy to a reproducible 150‑item NetOps sample. All artifacts and analysis were archived under preregistration contamination-audit-netops-2026-v1 (preregistration SHA‑256: 9a5e11c5b2b1c14c2a4a874a7ad0b9f215f8477a7becf4eb6dd1c0ff6a00ae7a). Execution used a single hosted model (declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini") and a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). The run produced zero preregistered high‑confidence contamination flags and identical validator pass counts for baseline and guarded episodes (baseline = 150/150, guarded = 150/150). The paired contingency is n11=150, n10=n01=n00=0, giving a paired difference = 0.0 percentage points (95% bootstrap CI [0.0,0.0]); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Critically, artifact evidence shows the preregistered estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) was rendered untestable/degenerate under the executed generation semantics because the pipeline reused a single shared generation per item (independent_condition_generation = false) and the confirmatory sample comprised provenance‑stable synthetic tasks (task source_identifier prefix "synthetic-netops:"). We (1) document the preregistration→execution reconciliation with concrete artifact paths and SHA‑256 hashes, (2) explain why the execution choices produced a degenerate paired comparison, and (3) give artifact‑anchored, implementable recommendations (provenance‑rich public sampling, independent per‑condition generation, per‑item overlap persistence, multi‑model replication, paraphrase‑sensitive detectors) to make future contamination audits sensitive to leakage in web‑sourced benchmarks.

sections.introduction:
Motivation. Large language models are increasingly applied to NetOps tasks (intent→configuration translation, automated repair). Benchmarks influence operational decisions; contamination (benchmark items present in model training corpora) or low‑complexity templating can inflate measured capability. Surveys call for contamination‑aware audits combining deterministic detectors and deterministic or formal validators.

Research question and contribution. We preregistered and executed an artifact‑anchored audit to answer: under conservative deterministic contamination detectors and a preregistered guarded exclusion policy, how many high‑confidence flags occur in a reproducible 150‑item sample and how much does applying those controls change validator‑measured success for a single hosted LLM? Our contributions are: (1) a full preregistration and execution archive (study_id = contamination-audit-netops-2026-v1; preregistration SHA‑256 = 9a5e11c5b2b1c14c2a4a874a7ad0b9f215f8477a7becf4eb6dd1c0ff6a00ae7a); (2) exact, artifact‑verified confirmatory statistics for Npairs = 150 based on deterministic validator traces; (3) an explicit preregistration→execution reconciliation (artifact‑anchored) that explains why the run produced a degenerate null and prescribes concrete, implementable changes to increase audit sensitivity.

Key bounded claim. The null result (zero flags, no paired discordance) applies to this specific execution regime (provenance‑stable synthetic sampling + shared generation semantics) and does not imply absence of contamination in independent web‑sourced public benchmarks.
sections.related_work:
LLM→NetOps and generate–validate pipelines. Prior works show LLMs can generate device configurations and plausible repairs; integrating formal validators or iterative validate–repair loops improves average repair quality (e.g., recent benchmark and system papers). Formal network verification tools (Header Space Analysis, localized subspecification methods) are practical oracles for reachability and policy checks and are often used in generate–validate workflows.

Evaluation validity and contamination critiques. Meta‑analyses and surveys document contamination and construct‑validity risks in LLM benchmarks and recommend deterministic fingerprinting, fuzzy n‑gram overlap, provenance tracing, and explicit reporting. Our audit implements a conservative subset of these defenses within a preregistered confirmatory design and differs from prior studies by (a) freezing the analysis executor and exclusion rules before execution and (b) providing an artifact‑anchored reconciliation when execution semantics made the primary test uninformative.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration summary. The experiment was preregistered (study_id = contamination-audit-netops-2026-v1) and froze estimands, detectors, exclusion rules, sampling plan, and analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1). The preregistered primary estimand was the paired success‑rate difference (guarded − baseline) evaluated by an exact McNemar two‑sided test plus a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Planned confirmatory accounting: task_count = 150 items; planned_episode_count = 300; maximum_model_calls = 300.

Detectors and guarded policy. The preregistered detector suite implemented three deterministic heuristics: (1) exact normalized token equality; (2) fuzzy 5‑gram shingle overlap with preregistered high‑confidence threshold ≥ 0.80 (and lower thresholds for sensitivity checks at 0.65 and 0.50); (3) provenance timestamp heuristics comparing item timestamps/DOIs to public archive dates. The guarded policy deterministically excluded only high‑confidence flags (exact OR 5‑gram ≥ 0.80) and replaced them via deterministic retemplating + topology augmentation subject to a preregistered embedding similarity safeguard (cosine ≥ 0.85). The detector persistence policy (to limit artifact size) persisted per‑item fuzzy overlap tables only when threshold crossings or replacements occurred; this behavior is documented in the execution transformation manifest (path: execution/transformation_manifest.json) and is reflected in the absence of a global per‑item overlap artifact when no threshold crossings occurred (see Results). The archived contamination plan and detection procedures are included in the preregistration artifact (preregistration SHA‑256 above).

Sampling, generation semantics, and validators. To ensure reproducibility the preregistration allowed deterministic synthetic task generation. The executed run used deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 to produce the confirmatory sample. Each task encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, allowed_touched_fields, and an explicit intent. The deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) is the deterministic oracle: parse candidate configuration, apply to modeled device state, and check required_final_state plus workflow constraints; it emits a binary pass/fail and detailed traces archived per episode.

Preregistration→execution reconciliation (compact mapping). The reviewer requested a concise mapping of preregistered → executed values with artifact substantiation. We provide the compact mapping below (all executed artifact paths refer to files in the archived bundle):

- benchmark_scope (preregistered): four public OpenAlex datasets: https://openalex.org/W7157506260; https://openalex.org/W4404602270; https://openalex.org/W4404534210; https://openalex.org/W7166900660. (See preregistration artifact; preregistration SHA‑256 = 9a5e11c5b2b1c14c2a4a874a7ad0b9f215f8477a7becf4eb6dd1c0ff6a00ae7a.)

- sampled items (executed): provenance‑stable synthetic tasks (source_identifier prefix "synthetic-netops:") generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Evidence: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (sha256 = b7c08599e3f96d8d5605a18f8f973e0707d7224327eeed7bde78c0d34cb83e55).

- planned_maximum_model_calls (preregistered): 300 (two per item). Executed model_calls_used: 150. Evidence: execution_manifest and execution/model_configuration.json (execution/model_configuration.json sha256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820) and execution/raw_results.jsonl (sha256 = 5337998d1d86aca507f77659d75cc9487cf3d87a157ed5044b8a9d5ff79b5586).

- independent_condition_generation (preregistered): allowed (boolean). Executed: false (shared_initial_candidate semantics), which caused single shared generation per item and reduced independent trials. Evidence: execution/model_configuration.json (sha256 above) and deterministic_reconciliation artifact (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json sha256 = 57c70942a9ffa93f7a2cb0c87c8996fcf12d516066a3ce6b5dcbb33add40b8b8) showing model_calls_used = 150.

- detector persistence policy (preregistered): persist per‑item overlap tables only when threshold crossings or replacements occur. Evidence: preregistered detection_procedures in the preregistration artifact (preregistration SHA‑256 above) and the executed transformation manifest (execution/transformation_manifest.json) documenting the implemented persistence rule; because no threshold crossings occurred, analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty (sha256 = 389227f0d1e81239c7498abd4944a04c59c92c5fa042b990e332796cd61c3222).

These artifact paths and SHA‑256 hashes allow direct verification of the executed choices and their effects on observable discordance.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and core statistics. Execution completed planned_episode_count = 300 (150 item pairs) with completed_episode_count = 300 and failed_episode_count = 0. Provider call accounting shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 150 and completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 150 (model_calls_used = 150); thereby a single shared generation per item was used (evidence: execution/raw_results.jsonl sha256 = 5337998d1d86aca507f77659d75cc9487cf3d87a157ed5044b8a9d5ff79b5586; execution/model_configuration.json sha256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820).

Contamination detectors. The preregistered detector suite produced zero high‑confidence contamination flags for the executed sample; analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty (sha256 = 389227f0d1e81239c7498abd4944a04c59c92c5fa042b990e332796cd61c3222). Because the detector persistence policy archived detailed per‑item fuzzy overlap tables only when threshold crossings or replacements occurred, no global per‑item overlap distribution artifact was persisted for this run; this absence is an explicit artifact of the implementation and is documented in the transformation manifest (execution/transformation_manifest.json) and the preregistration detection_procedures (preregistration SHA‑256 above). Consequently, we report the artifact‑verified absence of preregistered high‑confidence flags rather than providing per‑item overlap scores for this execution.

Validator outcomes and confirmatory analysis. The deterministic validator returned pass for all baseline episodes (baseline_success_count = 150/150; baseline_success_rate = 1.0) and for all guarded episodes (guarded_success_count = 150/150; guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv sha256 = c2ba9cdb5d0938eae910129ba511eadf309319e6e05b36d9e3b4860032deb80e) is:

n11 = 150, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0.

Primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) = 0.0 percentage points. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.0]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. All per‑episode validator traces and raw model responses are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl sha256 above and execution/scoring/ examples in the archive) and underpin these numbers.

Representative diagnostic. Representative episode pair-000001 (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json; example entries archived) illustrates identical normalized_response and normalized_reference_answer and detailed validator_trace fields (parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration) that demonstrate the validator semantics used to produce binary outcomes.
sections.discussion:
Why the confirmatory test was degenerate. The artifact record shows two execution choices jointly rendered the preregistered paired test uninformative: (1) the confirmatory sample comprised provenance‑stable synthetic tasks (source_identifier prefix "synthetic-netops:") generated deterministically (evidence: execution/task_manifest.jsonl sha256 = b7c08599e3f96d8d5605a18f8f973e0707d7224327eeed7bde78c0d34cb83e55); and (2) the pipeline executed with independent_condition_generation = false (shared_initial_candidate semantics) so baseline and guarded episodes reused a single model generation per item when no exclusions occurred (evidence: execution/model_configuration.json sha256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820 and deterministic_reconciliation sha256 = 57c70942a9ffa93f7a2cb0c87c8996fcf12d516066a3ce6b5dcbb33add40b8b8). Under these conditions, absent any high‑confidence flags there is no independent generation noise to produce discordant pairs (n10 or n01), so the paired estimand is exactly zero by construction.

Detector persistence and interpretability tradeoffs. The detector implementation archived detailed per‑item fuzzy overlap tables only when threshold crossings or replacements occurred (execution/transformation_manifest.json documents this persistence rule). Because no threshold crossings occurred, no global overlap distribution was persisted and post‑hoc reconstruction of overlap distances to the high‑confidence threshold is impossible from the current archive. This implementation choice reduced stored artifact volume but limited interpretability; we therefore recommend persisting full per‑item overlap scores in future audits regardless of threshold crossings so sensitivity curves and min/median/max distances to thresholds can be reported.

Practical recommendations (artifact‑anchored). To make future preregistered contamination audits informative for web‑sourced benchmarks we recommend the following implementable changes (all feasible within the archived execution framework): (A) sample provenance‑rich public items (URLs/DOIs/timestamps) so provenance heuristics can meaningfully flag pretraining‑era items; (B) set independent_condition_generation = true to force independent per‑condition generations (recordable in execution/model_configuration.json) and increase the chance of observing generation‑level discordance; (C) persist per‑item fuzzy 5‑gram overlap scores for all items (new artifact e.g., analysis/contamination_scores.csv) rather than only on threshold crossings; (D) expand to multiple model instances and independent seeds to reveal cross‑model signals and increase power; (E) add paraphrase‑sensitive detectors and human adjudication for borderline cases. Each recommendation follows directly from the recorded artifacts: model_calls_used = 150 (execution manifest), an empty analysis/contamination_summary.csv (sha256 = 389227f0...), and the lack of a per‑item overlap table in the archive.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired contamination audit. For the executed regime—provenance‑stable synthetic sampling and shared generation semantics—the preregistered conservative detectors produced no high‑confidence flags and the guarded policy made no changes; validator pass counts were identical (150/150 baseline and guarded). Artifact evidence demonstrates the primary confirmatory estimand was rendered untestable/degenerate under these execution choices; the null result therefore does not generalize to web‑sourced public benchmarks. We provide a precise preregistration→execution reconciliation (artifact paths and SHA‑256 hashes above), explain the mechanistic cause of degeneracy, and present concrete, implementable changes to increase audit sensitivity. All execution, validation, and analysis artifacts supporting these statements are archived in the execution bundle and listed in the Disclosure Statement below.

limitations: Single‑model execution (gpt‑5-mini) — results do not generalize across other LLM families, sizes, or training corpora.

Sampled items in this run were provenance‑stable synthetic/deterministically generated tasks (source_identifier prefix "synthetic-netops:"); absence of high‑confidence flags here may not reflect contamination prevalence in real‑world, web‑crawled benchmarks.

Generation semantics used shared_initial_candidate across baseline and guarded conditions (independent_condition_generation = false), producing identical model outputs when no exclusions occurred and thus limiting sensitivity to interventions that rely on independent re‑generation.

Contamination detection used conservative lexical heuristics (exact match and fuzzy 5‑gram overlap); paraphrase leakage or subtler memorization may escape these heuristics and require paraphrase‑robust detectors and human adjudication.

Passing deterministic_netops_validator_v5 indicates satisfaction of the checked functional constraints but does not imply comprehensive production readiness or absence of semantic regressions outside the validator's scope.
